Its launch figures show small gains on broad tests, for example MMLU-Pro 76.4 against 75.8 (e2). The 35.1 figure he cited matches 2.0 Flash's LiveCodeBench score. But some gains were not tiny: HiddenMath rose from 52 to 63 (e3), and 2.0 Flash is far ahead of 1.5 Flash, its direct predecessor. The broader claim that 18 months of results were incremental is contradicted on some measures: in September 2024, OpenAI's o1 jumped from 12% to 74% on the AIME math exam compared with GPT-4o (e4).
limitations: The Gemini figures come from a secondary aggregator that reproduces Google's table.

our_interpretation: Two parts: (a) Gemini 2.0 at its December 11, 2024 launch was only modestly better than Gemini 1.5 on published benchmarks; (b) frontier model results over the prior 18 months (about June 2023 to December 2024) showed incremental rather than large jumps.
For (a), I compare Google's launch figures for Gemini 2.0 Flash with the best Gemini 1.5 model, 1.5 Pro, as he appears to. I also note the Flash-to-Flash comparison.
The 34.3 to 35.1 figures appear to match LiveCodeBench (a coding benchmark) in Google's launch table, not LiveBench.
criteria.support_condition: Gemini 2.0 shows only small gains over Gemini 1.5 across most published benchmarks, and no frontier release in the 18 months made a large jump.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Gemini 2.0 shows large gains over Gemini 1.5 on most benchmarks, or a frontier release in the 18-month window made a large jump on major benchmarks.
